newsitem.title: UK: EMAP says succession issue not settled.
newsitem.headline: EMAP says succession issue not settled.

text.p: EMAP chief executive Robin Miller said on Monday that the question of who succeeds Sir John Hoskyns as chairman next year is still to be resolved.
"A plan hasn't been decided by the board," Miller told Reuters, adding that the company was committed to settling the matter "in good time" ahead of Hoskyns' retirement in 1998.
EMAP managing director David Arculus, seen as a rival to Miller for the chairmanship, announced on Monday that he was joining United News & Media as its chief operating officer.
"I got offered a job about three times the size of the one I was doing at EMAP," Arculus told Reuters.
EMAP suffered a damaging boardroom split last year which culminated in the ousting of two rebel non-executive directors.
Hoskyns at the time denied he backed Miller as his successor and dismissed talk of a rift between Miller and Arculus.
Miller said he had his differences with Arculus but said that the partnership had worked well and added that the departure of the managing director was a blow.

"...This is a pretty major change and not necessarily of our choosing," Miller said of the loss of Arculus, who joined EMAP back in 1972. "But he's been offered a good job and he has accepted it," he added.
Miller said there were no immediate plans to replace Arculus but did not rule out an appointment in the longer term.
He said that the company was seeking to recruit non-executive directors as deputy chairman Richard Winfrey was due to step down this year and Hoskyns in 1998.
Arculus will have operational responsibility at United News for consumer publishing, broadcasting and entertainment, and trade magazines and exhibitions.
United said the appointment completed the management team assembled at the company since its merger with MAI last year.
Arculus noted that United's acquisition last October of international exhibitions group Blenheim meant its business services division alone was more or less the size of EMAP.
He said he was looking forward to the change to work in television and national newspapers, two of United's key areas.
He was encouraged by the nine percent month-on-month circulation rise posted by The Express newspaper in January. The title has been revamped as it seeks to end a long-running sales decline.
He also saw potential for down-market tabolid the Daily Star, which lags way behind its rivals the Sun and Daily Mirror.
"I think the Daily Star has got a good position in the younger male market," he said, noting his success at EMAP with the FHM magazine aimed at just that group of consumers.
